title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages. V is a real Euclidean plane with quadratic form e. The underline-ω is the two-element torsor of orientations of V. For each orientation ω there is a complex structure u_ω (rotation by +90°). The complexification splits as V_C ≅ ∏_ω V_(ω), giving the two isotropic lines, i.e. the 'circular points'. Σ is the projective line P(V) of lines F ⊂ V, viewed as a scheme or analytically.

This page introduces the following.

(i) O_Σ(1). Grothendieck's convention is used: P(V) parametrises rank-1 quotients, so the fibre at F is O_F(1) = V/F.

(ii) The associated principal G_m- (or C*-) bundle PΣ. Its fibre is O(1)_x minus zero. Here Grothendieck's notation E^* means E \ {0}, as in C^*.

(iii) Canonical descriptions of these fibres, labelled (18):
- O_F(1) = V/F.
- By exterior product, F ⊗ V/F ≅ det V. Write R(ω) := R ∧^{±1} ω for the orientation line, i.e. the line induced from the ±1-torsor ω; then det V ≅ R(ω).
- Hence O_F(1) ≅ F^∨(ω) := F^∨ ∧^{±1} ω.
- Using e, O_F(1) ≅ F^⊥, via the projection F^⊥ → V/F.

(19) Consequently (PΣ)_F ≅ (V/F)^* ≅ (F^∨(ω))^* ≅ (F^⊥)^*, compatibly with the C*-actions (C* acts on F^∨ contragrediently).

(20) Using the metric to identify F^∨ with F, one also gets (PΣ)_x ≅ (F(ω))^* ≅ (F^⊥)^*.

The next page assembles these into global isomorphisms PΣ ≅ V \ 0 and PΣ ≅ V(ω) \ 0, sending (F, ξ) to the unique lift of ξ in F^⊥. It compares them via the canonical V ≅ V^∨(ω) (exterior product) and V ≅ V^∨ (form e). The result is an isomorphism V ≅ V(ω) inducing the involution F ↦ F^⊥ on Σ, equivariant for the dihedral/orthogonal group D.

Purpose: a careful, orientation-twist-aware description of the circle of real directions and its C*-torsor (the punctured tautological line). This is presumably a model for tangential directions / tangential base points and their D-symmetry, inside the Teichmüller-groupoid notes.
errors: The identifications O_F(1) = V/F ≅ F^⊥ and F^∨(ω) ≅ F^⊥ hold only for non-isotropic F. The composite F^⊥ → V → V/F is an isomorphism iff F ∩ F^⊥ = 0. Over the real points of Σ (a definite form) this is fine. But as stated 'dans le contexte des schémas' it fails at the closed point corresponding to the pair of isotropic (circular) lines. Canonically and everywhere one has F^⊥ ≅ (V/F)^∨ = O_F(-1) instead. Grothendieck seems aware ('pour le moment ...'), but the text does not restrict the domain.
Equation numbers (18), (19) are reused, clashing with (18), (19) on the previous page. This is a bookkeeping slip in the draft.

ideas.what: O(1) on P(V) defined as the universal quotient V/F (Grothendieck's convention), with F ⊗ O(1) ≅ det V
ideas.modern_name: Euler sequence / tautological quotient line bundle on a projective line
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; this convention is Grothendieck's own (EGA II)

ideas.what: Twisting by the orientation torsor: R(ω) = R ∧^{±1} ω, det V ≅ R(ω), O_F(1) ≅ F^∨(ω)
ideas.modern_name: orientation line / line bundle induced from a ±1-torsor (contracted product)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (orientation sheaf; contracted products of torsors as in Giraud)

ideas.what: Principal C*- (G_m-) bundle PΣ attached to O(1), with fibres described as F^⊥ \ 0, giving PΣ ≅ V \ 0 via the metric
ideas.modern_name: punctured tautological line bundle; G_m-torsor of a line bundle

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear algebra on a projective line over a Euclidean plane, with careful bookkeeping of orientation twists. It is preparatory material for the D-symmetry of tangential directions, with no new result or unexpected connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: '(ou les quelques complications complexes, disons, avec la topologie habituelles' likely reads '(ou les groupes complexes, disons, avec la topologie habituelle — pour le moment on travaille plus (?) dans le contexte des schémas ...)'.
Line 2: 'comme [fibré] droite projective associée à un vectoriel bien déterminé'. 'fibré' is struck; the machine's '[-droites-]' is part of 'droite projective'.
The superscript '*' in (19)/(20), e.g. (V/F)^*, (F^⊥)^*, denotes the complement of 0 (as in C^*), not the dual space.
'opérant sur F̌ par contragrédiente via action sur F': reading 'contragrédiente' seems right.
Equation label at bottom: a struck-out label precedes '(20)'.
